@graph.name: Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS
@graph.description: Google text-to-speech model for expressive long-form narration and multi-speaker dialogue.

acceptedAnswer.text: Google's text-to-speech model for expressive, studio-style narration, regional accents and multi-speaker dialogue. It takes text and returns audio; it is not the Gemini Live API.

mainEntity.name: What is the Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS model ID?

acceptedAnswer.text: Use gemini-3.8-flash-tts in the Gemini API. It is different from the general-purpose gemini-3.8-flash model.

mainEntity.name: How much does Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Through December 31, 2026, Google lists $0.50 per million text input tokens and $9 per million generated audio output tokens on Standard paid API; from January 1, 2027 the published rates are $1 and $18.

mainEntity.name: How much is a minute of generated speech?

acceptedAnswer.text: At Google's 25 output audio tokens per second, 60 seconds is 1,500 audio tokens. That costs approximately $0.0135 at the introductory Standard rate, before text input charges.

mainEntity.name: Does Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS support multiple speakers?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. In a single request Google supports up to two configured speakers using prebuilt voices. Each dialogue turn needs a matching speech_metadata.speaker value.

mainEntity.name: Can I control speaking style and add pauses?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Use speech_metadata.style for turn-level performance and inline tags such as <short pause> or <laugh> for point-in-time vocal events.

mainEntity.name: Does Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS support Arabic?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Google's supported-language list includes Standard Arabic and Egyptian Arabic; the model automatically detects input language. Actual pronunciation should be evaluated with your own transcripts.

mainEntity.name: What is the context window and output limit?

acceptedAnswer.text: Google documents an 8,192-token input limit and a 16,384-token output serving limit. Audio duration is billed by generated audio tokens, not ordinary text output.

mainEntity.name: Is Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS the same as Gemini Live?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Flash TTS converts a supplied transcript to audio, whereas the Live API is intended for interactive streaming, multimodal conversation.

mainEntity.name: Flash TTS vs Flash-Lite TTS: which should I choose?

acceptedAnswer.text: Choose Flash TTS for maximum vocal nuance, difficult pronunciations, dialect coverage and long narration. Choose Flash-Lite TTS for lower-cost, high-throughput or everyday voice production; both share the same request schema.
